grounding.derivation: VerifyLeader promises to ensure leadership and supports avoiding stale reads. Suffrage distinguishes voters from nonvoting replication recipients. feedback.answered: A1 formation: dispatchLogs assigns current-term indices, stores logs, and only after StoreLogs succeeds reports the local match and wakes replicators. replicateTo and pipelineDecode accept successful replies after checking for a response term newer than the request; updateLastAppended reports the last request entry to the replication state's commitment object. commitment counts only configured voters, takes the majority order statistic and advances monotonically only at or beyond this leader's startIndex. leaderLoop consumes its notification, updates committed configuration and gathers committed inflight logs. processLogs sends command/barrier tuples to the asynchronous FSM worker; its lastApplied update means dispatch progress, whereas applySingle completes the future after FSM.Apply returns. A2 authority: follower timeout checks local voter eligibility; a candidate uses a campaign-local reply channel, electSelf increments and persists term through setCurrentTerm and requests one vote per configured voter, and requestVote checks membership, known leader, term, prior vote and log freshness before persisting a grant. A new leader allocates a fresh commitment object and dispatches a no-op. On loss of leadership it closes replication stop channels and fails pending log and verification futures; replication objects retain their own commitment references, so the observed accounting path is not an unconditional write into a subsequent leader's fresh commitment. Configuration admission waits for the previous configuration and a current-term entry to be committed, then changes the accounting voter set. Followers reject older AppendEntries terms and mismatched predecessor terms, replace conflicting suffixes, roll latest configuration back when truncation crosses it, and dispatch up to the received commit bound. The FSM interface independently states that Apply is called after majority commitment. These are observed mechanisms and interface requirements, not proof of their composition.

formation.explanation: Leader stores indexed current-term logs and reports its own match; per-peer replication verifies successful responses and accounts last sent entries or installed snapshot. Current voter majority and tenure startIndex select commit advancement. Leader propagates commit through append requests; followers check term and predecessor, reconcile entries, select a local bound and dispatch through processLogs. FSM execution is asynchronous; client success follows actual Apply completion.

context.explanation: Follower timeouts and transfer trigger campaigns over latest voters. Pre-vote checks plausibility without persisting term; actual election increments durable term, persists votes and uses log freshness. Campaign replies are private to the attempt. Leader entry creates fresh commitment and workers; higher-term RPC/reply, lease loss or self-removal ends authority, stops old workers and fails pending futures. Install/startup recover log/snapshot and configuration context; transfer catches target up before TimeoutNow.

connection.explanation: Support is eligible within the captured leader tenure and current voter set. Fresh tenure accounting and a current-term no-op prevent simply reusing old majority indexes; old workers retain old commitment/stepDown channels. Persisted history constrains votes, while a new leader reconciles follower suffixes before local consumption. Configuration changes are admitted one at a time after current-term commitment and immediately reinterpret voter support. Already dispatched FSM work is distinct from remaining inflight futures, so leadership loss cannot imply rollback. Snapshot recovery reinstates applied prefix/configuration and can supply catch-up support.

feedback.answered: For ordinary append catch-up with accurate persisted-log metadata and a normal matching-prefix/divergent-suffix history, the sender does not first send an arbitrary early matching batch. A new tenure starts nextIndex at the leader end plus one. Rejection backs up one position, or jumps to a shorter follower end plus one. For a retained divergence at d, predecessor checks reject until predecessor d-1; the next request starts at d and truncates the conflicting suffix before applying the commit bound. A shorter follower has no suffix beyond the end hint. Successful ordinary replication catches up through its target before enabling the pipeline, which starts at the last successful nextIndex. Dedicated heartbeats carry no commit index. Thus the apparent receiver-only gap does not establish a defect under the selected normal sender history. This is a sourced conditional explanation, not an executed negative result or proof of all commit paths.

grounding.derivation: VerifyLeader promises to ensure leadership and supports avoiding stale reads. Suffrage distinguishes voters from nonvoting replication recipients. The implementation deliberately derives the verification threshold from quorumSize (counting voters) and describes completion as quorum agreement; eligibility must therefore be consistent between that threshold and the support counted. Counting a nonvoter cannot establish missing voter agreement. This is a local support-eligibility duty, not an assertion that every partition immediately ends leadership or that absent support owes success.
grounding.applicability: Established multi-voter leader with fixed mixed-suffrage configuration; fresh verification with independently identified acknowledgements.
alternatives: A separately voter-filtered lease can eventually remove authority, but its timer is not a substitute for eligible support in each verification tally.

feedback.answered: A1 formation: dispatchLogs assigns current-term indices, stores logs, and only after StoreLogs succeeds reports the local match and wakes replicators. replicateTo and pipelineDecode accept successful replies after checking for a response term newer than the request; updateLastAppended reports the last request entry to the replication state's commitment object. commitment counts only configured voters, takes the majority order statistic and advances monotonically only at or beyond this leader's startIndex. leaderLoop consumes its notification, updates committed configuration and gathers committed inflight logs. processLogs sends command/barrier tuples to the asynchronous FSM worker; its lastApplied update means dispatch progress, whereas applySingle completes the future after FSM.Apply returns. A2 authority: follower timeout checks local voter eligibility; a candidate uses a campaign-local reply channel, electSelf increments and persists term through setCurrentTerm and requests one vote per configured voter, and requestVote checks membership, known leader, term, prior vote and log freshness before persisting a grant. A new leader allocates a fresh commitment object and dispatches a no-op. On loss of leadership it closes replication stop channels and fails pending log and verification futures; replication objects retain their own commitment references, so the observed accounting path is not an unconditional write into a subsequent leader's fresh commitment. Configuration admission waits for the previous configuration and a current-term entry to be committed, then changes the accounting voter set. Followers reject older AppendEntries terms and mismatched predecessor terms, replace conflicting suffixes, roll latest configuration back when truncation crosses it, and dispatch up to the received commit bound. The FSM interface independently states that Apply is called after majority commitment. These are observed mechanisms and interface requirements, not proof of their composition.

surface:Raft.appendEntries: commit advancement uses min(LeaderCommitIndex, local last index), while setNewLogs limits requests to MaxAppendEntries. Dedicated heartbeat requests have LeaderCommitIndex zero and do not supply this trigger; predecessor matching and conflict truncation are contrary protections. Establish a same-history producer path rather than injecting arbitrary entries.

formation.explanation: Leader stores indexed current-term logs and reports its own match; per-peer replication verifies successful responses and accounts last sent entries or installed snapshot. Current voter majority and tenure startIndex select commit advancement. Leader propagates commit through append requests; followers check term and predecessor, reconcile entries, select a local bound and dispatch through processLogs. FSM execution is asynchronous; client success follows actual Apply completion.

context.explanation: Follower timeouts and transfer trigger campaigns over latest voters. Pre-vote checks plausibility without persisting term; actual election increments durable term, persists votes and uses log freshness. Campaign replies are private to the attempt. Leader entry creates fresh commitment and workers; higher-term RPC/reply, lease loss or self-removal ends authority, stops old workers and fails pending futures. Install/startup recover log/snapshot and configuration context; transfer catches target up before TimeoutNow.

connection.explanation: Support is eligible within the captured leader tenure and current voter set. Fresh tenure accounting and a current-term no-op prevent simply reusing old majority indexes; old workers retain old commitment/stepDown channels. Persisted history constrains votes, while a new leader reconciles follower suffixes before local consumption. Configuration changes are admitted one at a time after current-term commitment and immediately reinterpret voter support. Already dispatched FSM work is distinct from remaining inflight futures, so leadership loss cannot imply rollback. Snapshot recovery reinstates applied prefix/configuration and can supply catch-up support.

feedback.answered: For ordinary append catch-up with accurate persisted-log metadata and a normal matching-prefix/divergent-suffix history, the sender does not first send an arbitrary early matching batch. A new tenure starts nextIndex at the leader end plus one. Rejection backs up one position, or jumps to a shorter follower end plus one. For a retained divergence at d, predecessor checks reject until predecessor d-1; the next request starts at d and truncates the conflicting suffix before applying the commit bound. A shorter follower has no suffix beyond the end hint. Successful ordinary replication catches up through its target before enabling the pipeline, which starts at the last successful nextIndex. Dedicated heartbeats carry no commit index. Thus the apparent receiver-only gap does not establish a defect under the selected normal sender history. This is a sourced conditional explanation, not an executed negative result or proof of all commit paths.
